newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Seven in chopper survive Colombian rebel attack.
newsitem.headline: Seven in chopper survive Colombian rebel attack.

text.p: At least seven people, initially feared dead, survived when the helicopter in which they were flying was shot down by leftist rebels in an oil-producing region of eastern Colombia, military sources said on Monday.
The army originally said all on board -- 25 soldiers and four civilian crew members -- died when the Russian-made Mi-17 chopper went down near the town of Arauquita in Arauca province on Sunday.

"We have confirmed four soldiers survived and we have three surviving crew members," said army chief Gen. Manuel Jose Bonett, in Arauca to head the operation to recover the bodies of the dead and track down the National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels blamed for the attack.
"The area has now been secured and air reinforcements have been brought in," he added.
An army spokeswoman said a final death toll was not available as it had not been established exactly how many people were on board the helicopter.
President Ernesto Samper condemned the incident, calling it an "act of terror and cowardice."

"Some subversives are afraid of peace and of sitting down at the negotiating table to achieve what they think they can achieve by the blind use of weapons," he said, referring to his plans to launch a new peace process to end Colombia's three-decade-old guerrilla uprising.
Political analysts believe those plans are now in tatters following a spate of rebel assaults in the last three weeks.

The four surviving soldiers made their way to a military post late on Sunday. Two of them had extensive burns. Three crew members were discovered alive by an army ground patrol near the crash site on Monday, Bonett tolds reporters.

The ELN, Colombia's second largest guerrilla force set up by radical Roman Catholic priests in 1966, shot the helicopter down as it flew over the site where guerrillas had earlier blown up the pipeline serving Occidental Petroleum Corp's Cano Limon field, the army said.
An army spokeswoman said it was still not known how the rebels shot the chopper down. The ELN claimed in the past that it had a number of surface-to-air missiles.

The downing of the helicopter was one of the worst rebel attacks since Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) insurgents overran a military base in Putumayo province in August, killing 31 soldiers and taking 60 prisoner.
